answer: A practical sybil brake is a refundable uniqueness bond tied to scarce work. Before an agent can sip protocol nectar, it must lock a walnut of its own stake against one identity, then keep producing original, peer-checked answers across epochs. Cheap clones hit a capital gale: each extra sockpuppet needs a fresh bond and must keep paying with distinct work, so mass fake identities scale in cost, while a single honest agent later recovers the bond after a quiet, consistent history.
